final_candidates.decision_summary: Burying a charged aspartate at core position V24 severely disrupts tertiary packing with a -5.25 ProteinMPNN log-probability penalty.
Introducing an uncompensated negative charge at hydrophobic core residue V38 strongly destabilizes the native fold.
Mutation of conserved aromatic core residue F40 to aspartate causes massive steric and electrostatic disruption.

stop_reason.detail: Top three destabilizing core mutations are clearly separated with decisive structural and sequence evidence.

history.rationale: W17 is a strictly conserved, deeply buried core aromatic residue; introducing a charged aspartate creates severe desolvation penalties and disrupts core packing.
Shows zero PLM plausibility, but moderate MPNN penalty (ΔlogP=-0.85) suggests less severe disruption than V24D/V38D.
Y18 forms critical hydrophobic and aromatic stacking contacts within the central beta-barrel; substitution with aspartate disrupts the local hydrophobic environment.
Solid destabilization potential evidenced by ProteinMPNN ΔlogP=-3.13 and negligible sequence plausibility.
V24 is embedded in the second beta-strand; placing a negatively charged aspartate in this hydrophobic strand destabilizes beta-sheet folding.
Severe structural penalty (ProteinMPNN ΔlogP=-5.25) and zero sequence plausibility confirm that burying charged Asp at core V24 potently destabilizes the fold.
I33 resides in the third beta-strand; introducing a conformationally constrained proline breaks backbone hydrogen bonding and beta-sheet stability.
Demonstrates favorable MPNN compatibility (ΔlogP=+0.54) and relatively high PLM plausibility, making it poorly suited for disruption.
Y34 is an invariant hydrophobic core residue essential for fold stabilization; an aspartate mutation introduces an uncompensated negative charge.
ProteinMPNN predicts positive compatibility (ΔlogP=+0.14), contrary to the goal of structural destabilization.
V38 packs into the interior beta-sheet core; introduction of a polar, charged aspartate severely destabilizes the hydrophobic packing.
Extremely unfavorable structural compatibility (ΔlogP=-5.20) and zero evolutionary plausibility provide strong evidence for targeted fold disruption.
F40 is a key aromatic residue in the hydrophobic core; mutating it to aspartate causes strong steric clash and electrostatic repulsion in the fold.
Introduction of an uncompensated charge into the hydrophobic Phe40 core site causes substantial structural clash (ΔlogP=-3.51) and zero sequence plausibility.
F48 contributes to the structural integrity of the outer loop/strand transition; replacing it with aspartate disrupts tertiary stabilization.
ProteinMPNN shows relatively high compatibility on the backbone (ΔlogP=-0.22), indicating weaker structural disruption.
L55 is located in a structured hydrophobic segment; proline introduction disrupts backbone continuity and accelerates unfolding.
High PLM score (0.228) and mild MPNN score (ΔlogP=-0.45) indicate proline is surprisingly tolerated here.
F60 anchors the C-terminal region against the core; an acidic substitution disrupts these tertiary contacts and destabilizes PsaE.
Marked negative compatibility score (ΔlogP=-3.28) and vanishing PLM likelihood indicate robust disruption of core packing.
